interpretation: NEW post-photo-outcome exploratory environmental-context design; original mammal event results are known and this is NOT external outcome-blind validation or a causal environmental mechanism.
question: At near-equal astronomical daylength, how different are independently reanalyzed near-surface heat and rainfall between rising and falling seasons in the Serengeti? Does the sign rule out a simplistic warmer-falling-branch thermal explanation?

independent_source.provider: Open-Meteo ERA5 historical archive; underlying ECMWF ERA5
independent_source.locator_scope: PUBLIC COARSE REGIONAL REPRESENTATIVE CENTER, not any true/private physical camera coordinate. All cameras share the same regional climatic exposure in this limited screen.
independent_source.spatial_resolution: ERA5 approximately 0.25 degree; returned selected grid cell/elevation are model metadata, not exact source camera placement.
independent_source.citation: Open-Meteo historical ERA5 model; license/terms https://open-meteo.com/en/features; ERA5 climate reanalysis must be explicitly acknowledged.

astronomy_pairs.matched_according_to: symmetric solar calendar geometry (approximate fixed photoperiod at the regional latitude); NOT actual station-specific original event/photo roster

endpoints_frozen: delta_falling_minus_rising_trailing_30day_precipitation_mm (include target date and 29 preceding local dates)
yearwise descriptive mean and median of each difference, fraction strictly positive, and across all date pairs the median, 10th and 90th percentiles
each solstice year is one weather-cycle and 174 k pairs within that year are temporally autocorrelated; NO 522 iid independent tests
one deliberately simple check of signs relative to previously OBSERVED photographed-time effects, no weather-activity regression and no ecological p-value
limits: Regional ERA5 modeled air temperature and precipitation are not direct animal core-hour body heat or grass resources.
Only one climate cell and at most three annual cycles—cannot identify across-landscape generality or site-level climate-response coefficient.
No camera on-hour or detection q source; previous animal result remains recorded PHOTO time distribution only.
Environmental differences between the two branches do not identify thermal regulation or circadian memory without stronger design.
Keep all signs, no reverse-date selection after inspecting climate values.
